stops.Cryptic_Clue: Standing on legs in the Cathedral's shadow
stops.Hint_1: I was built to celebrate a King restored.
stops.Hint_2: Look for an open-air building resting on stone pillars in the main square.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Find the stone structure in Cathedral Square with the date 1671. This is the Guildhall. It was built in 1671 by the city to commemorate the restoration of King Charles II to the throne. It originally housed a butter market beneath it.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Three massive arches reach for the sky
stops.Hint_1: guarding the grave of a tragic Queen.
stops.Hint_2: Walk towards the largest building in the city.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Stand before the three massive gothic arches of the Cathedral. This is the spectacular West Front of Peterborough Cathedral. Katherine of Aragon Henry VIII's first wife is buried inside. Mary Queen of Scots was also buried here before being moved to Westminster!

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Where the river runs and taxes were paid
stops.Hint_1: look for the stone house where boats were delayed.
stops.Hint_2: Head down to the River Nene.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Find the small stone building right by the old town bridge. Built in the early 1700s this is the Old Customs House. This was where tolls were collected from the barges bringing goods up the River Nene from the Wash.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: A ringing sound in a village swallowed by the city. Find the pub where the highwayman drank.
stops.Hint_1: Head north to the old village of Werrington.
stops.Hint_2: Look for the traditional thatched pub.
stops.Unlock_Fact: We made it! The Blue Bell in Werrington is one of the oldest pubs in the area. Local legend claims it was a favourite haunt of highwaymen operating on the old Great North Road!

stops.Cryptic_Clue: The Lord Protector laid his head
stops.Hint_1: in a timber frame before he bled (or rather
stops.Hint_2: died of natural causes).
stops.Unlock_Fact: Find the heavily timbered house near the cathedral. Look for the house with the plaque for Oliver Cromwell. This is Oliver Cromwell's House. He lived here for 10 years before he led the Parliamentarian army against King Charles I. It's one of the few surviving residences of Cromwell.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: A massive gatehouse of brick and stone
stops.Hint_1: where monks once walked and scholars now roam.
stops.Hint_2: Walk south of the cathedral to find a massive medieval gate.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Look for the large brick archway leading into the school grounds. This is the Ely Porta completed in 1397. It was the main gatehouse to the medieval monastery. Today it forms part of the King's School Ely.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Where barley was soaked by the river's edge
stops.Hint_1: find the grand brick building by the water's ledge.
stops.Hint_2: Head down the hill to the River Great Ouse.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Look for the massive brick building right on the riverbank. This is The Maltings. Built in 1868 it was a massive industrial brewery complex where barley was malted for local beer production making use of the river for transport.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: The closest pint to the Bishop's seat. Find the tavern where the stonemasons meet.
stops.Hint_1: Head back towards the front of the Cathedral.
stops.Hint_2: Look for the pub literally right next to the Cathedral entrance.
stops.Unlock_Fact: We made it! The Minster Tavern is practically in the Cathedral's front garden. It's built on the site of the original monks' alehouse and generations of stonemasons drank here while building the cathedral.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Where a future Lord Protector learned to read
stops.Hint_1: in a building born from a Norman need.
stops.Hint_2: Find the old stone building in the High Street.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Look for the small stone building that used to be a Grammar School. This is the Cromwell Museum housed in the former Huntingdon Grammar School. Both Oliver Cromwell and Samuel Pepys were educated in this very room!

stops.Cryptic_Clue: A bird of prey in the market square
stops.Hint_1: where Civil War soldiers would drink and swear.
stops.Hint_2: Look for a historic pub right on the Market Square.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Find the pub named after a hunting bird. This is The Falcon. It was famously used as the headquarters for Oliver Cromwell's cavalry during the English Civil War. You can still feel the history in the timber beams.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Six arches of stone span the divide
stops.Hint_1: linking two towns on the river's tide.
stops.Hint_2: Head down to the River Great Ouse.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Find the medieval stone bridge crossing the river. This beautiful six-arch stone bridge was built around 1332. It connects Huntingdon with Godmanchester and is one of the finest surviving medieval bridges in England.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: A royal saint lends his name to this coaching inn
stops.Hint_1: where Shakespeare's company might have been.
stops.Hint_2: Head back up the High Street to a grand hotel.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Look for the large coaching inn with a courtyard. We made it! The George Hotel is a historic coaching inn. It features a rare surviving galleried courtyard a style of inn where travelling theatre companies perhaps even Shakespeare's men used to perform plays.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: A place of prayer suspended over the flow
stops.Hint_1: one of only four such sights to show.
stops.Hint_2: Walk down to the river.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Find the tiny chapel built directly into the middle of the bridge. This is the St Ives Bridge Chapel built in 1426. It is one of only four surviving bridge chapels in the whole of England originally meant for travellers to pray for a safe journey.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Where farmers traded grain for gold
stops.Hint_1: find the grand hall
stops.Hint_2: imposing and bold.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Look for the most impressive civic building in the town centre. Find the building with the large pillars on the pavement. Built in 1864 this Corn Exchange reflects the massive agricultural wealth of the area. It was the central hub for farmers across the fens to negotiate the sale of their crops.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: He stands in bronze
stops.Hint_1: stern and tall
stops.Hint_2: watching over the market stall.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Look for the large statue in the main market square. Find the bronze statue of a man with a sword and a bible. This is a statue of Oliver Cromwell who lived in St Ives for five years. He was a local farmer here before rising to become the Lord Protector of England.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: After seeing his statue
stops.Hint_1: seek his name. Find the riverside pub with a civil war claim.
stops.Hint_2: Look for a pub near the river named after the statue you just saw.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Find the pub on the waterfront. We made it! The Oliver Cromwell pub. Given the town's strong connections to the man it's the perfect place to end the trail and review the history we've just walked through.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: One of the largest squares in the land
stops.Hint_1: where markets have thrived since the monks took a stand.
stops.Hint_2: Start in the very centre of town.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Find the massive open square surrounded by shops. This is the St Neots Market Square. At over 2 acres it's one of the largest market squares in England established by the monks of the local priory in the 12th century.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Spanning the Ouse
stops.Hint_1: connecting the shires
stops.Hint_2: built of stone to withstand the mires.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Walk west from the square towards the river. Find the main stone bridge crossing the Great Ouse. This three-arch stone bridge was completed in 1617. Before this bridge was built travellers had to rely on a precarious wooden bridge or a ferry to cross the river into Bedfordshire.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: No monks chant here in the modern day
stops.Hint_1: but the name remembers where they used to pray.
stops.Hint_2: Look for a modern community building near the river.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Find the building that shares its name with a monastery. This site sits on the land of the original St Neots Priory a massive monastery founded in 975 AD. The priory was dissolved by Henry VIII and almost nothing remains of it above ground today.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Horses were rested and weary men fed
stops.Hint_1: where coaches to London found a warm bed.
stops.Hint_2: Return near the square and look for an old coaching inn.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Look for the pub on the High Street. We made it! St Neots was a major stop on the Great North Road. The Coach House (and the nearby cross keys) were essential rest stops for the stagecoaches travelling between London and the North.
